d.d: The twelfth numeral symbol of the English alphabet, called el and written in the Latin script.
Abbreviation of litre or liter.
Abbreviation of Latinlibra (“pound (sterling)”).
Abbreviation of leaf.
Clipping of lol.
Initialism of large (of the manufactured size).
Initialism of left.
Initialism of low (variety of a language with limited prestige and official acceptance).
A mother tongue; someone's native language; own language.
Abbreviation of Lagrange point 1, located between the larger and smaller objects along a line connecting the two.
The first-level cache of a processor, closer to the processor than the second-level cache.
A second language (a language being learned, as opposed to a mother tongue).
Abbreviation of Lagrange point 2, located beyond the smaller object on a line passing through the centers of the smaller and larger objects.
The second-level cache of a processor, farther away from the processor than the first level cache.
d.x: In typical Intel chips L2 bandwidth is half of L1 bandwidth.

d.d: Abbreviation of Lagrange point 3, located 180 degrees away from the smaller object and slightly outside the smaller object's orbit around the larger object.
The third-level cache of a processor, farther away from the processor than the second-level cache.
The network layer in the seven-layer OSI network model.
Abbreviation of Lagrange point 4, located 60 degrees ahead of the smaller object along its orbit around the larger object.
Abbreviation of Lagrange point 5, located 60 degrees behind the smaller object along its orbit around the larger object.
Abbreviation of late.
